It has been electing representatives [[at-large]] to the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] since 1987 and earlier to the [[National Assembly (Second Philippine Republic)|National Assembly]] from 1943 to 1944.{{cite web |url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |title=Roster of Philippine legislators |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=March 15, 2021 |archive-date=March 16, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170316064243/http://congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |url-status=dead }} The district was first formed ahead of the [[1943 Philippine legislative election]] following the ratification of the [[Second Philippine Republic]] constitution which called for a unicameral legislature composed of delegates from all provinces and chartered cities in the country.{{cite web|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1943-constitution/ |title=The 1943 Constitution |publisher=[[Official Gazette (Philippines)]] |accessdate=March 15, 2021}} Bacolod, a chartered city since 1938, elected Francisco Zulueta to the [[National Assembly (Second Philippine Republic)|National Assembly]], who was joined by then-mayor Alfredo C. Yulo as an appointed second delegate.{{cite web|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1938/06/18/commonwealth-act-no-326/ |title=Commonwealth Act No. 326 |date=18 June 1938 |publisher=[[Official Gazette (Philippines)]] |accessdate=March 15, 2021}} The district became inactive following the restoration of the House of Representatives in 1945 when the city reverted to its old provincial constituency of [[Negros Occidental's 2nd congressional district]]. In the unicameral [[Batasang Pambansa]] that replaced the House, Bacolod was not entitled to its own separate representation despite being a highly-urbanized city. Instead, it formed part of the multi-member [[Western Visayas|Region VI]]'s at-large district for the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa|interim parliament]] from 1978 to 1984 and [[Negros Occidental's at-large congressional district|Negros Occidental's at-large district]] in the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa|regular parliament]] from 1984 to 1986. The city-wide electoral district was only restored in 1987 under a new constitution.{{cite web|url=https://www.chanrobles.com/ordinance.htm |title=The 1987 Constitution of the Republic of the Philippines |publisher=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library |accessdate=March 15, 2021}} The district is currently represented in the [[20th Congress of the Philippines|20th Congress]] is [[Albee Benitez]] of the [[Partido Federal ng Pilipinas]] (PFP). ==Representation history==
